confirmed_defect: Original controlling audit stopped only at max|R11^-1 R12|<=f yet claimed both full strong spectral block bounds. Coefficient control alone gives no control on R22. The active algorithm adds the necessary combined residual score.
independent_defect_witness: For a partitioned full-rank A=diag(1,M), k=1, f=1 and M>sqrt(2), X=0 passes the coefficient test while sigma_1(R11)=1<M/sqrt(2) and sigma_1(R22)=M>sqrt(2)sigma_2(A). This is a witness against coefficient-only partition sufficiency, not an assertion about greedy CPQR selecting the first column of that diagonal matrix.

repaired_interface.inputs: Full-column-rank real/complex A with m>=n, 0<=k<n, f>=1 and finite swap cap.
repaired_interface.score: X=R11^-1 R12; omega_i=||e_i* R11^-1||2; gamma_j=||R22(:,j)||2; s_ij=sqrt(|Xij|²+(omega_i gamma_j)²).
repaired_interface.selection: Preserve coefficient-first largest-violation branch; if none, largest combined score above f. Lexicographic ties. Restore triangular form by unitary transformations.
repaired_interface.success: All scores<=f; hence all |Xij|<=f. k=0 succeeds without swaps.
repaired_interface.guarantees: Exact-arithmetic volume ratio equals s_ij; at most binomial(n,k)-1 swaps; both spectral block comparisons retain g=sqrt(1+f²k(n-k)).

source_reading.title: Ming Gu and Stanley C. Eisenstat, Efficient Algorithms for Computing a Strong Rank-Revealing QR Factorization

source_reading.actually_read: Complete relevant Section 3 argument: Algorithms 3 and 4, Lemma 3.1 and its proof, Theorem 3.2 and its proof, printed pp.852–854. The beginning of Section 4 was read to distinguish the later efficient adaptive-rank algorithm; no whole-paper reading is claimed.
source_reading.notation_match: Paper uses omega_i=1/||row_i(Ak^-1)||2 and gamma_j/omega_i; draft names the row norm itself omega_i and multiplies. The scores agree.

independent_proof_checks: Volume ratio follows from determinant(Cprime*Cprime+gamma² e_i e_i*) with row inverse term; extension at zero coefficient uses the squared polynomial identity.
For alpha=||R22||2/sigma_k(R11)>0, R=D1W1 with D1=diag(R11,R22/alpha), W1=[[I,X],[0,alpha I]]. Top k singular values of D1 are those of R11; ||W1||²<=1+||X||F²+alpha²<=g².
D2=RW2 with D2=diag(alpha R11,R22), W2=[[alpha I,-X],[0,I]]. Last n-k singular values of D2 are those of R22 and ||W2||<=g. Product inequality yields the trailing comparison.
Strict volume growth works even at f=1; it yields finite subset bound, not a polynomial complexity claim.
Kahan-style CPQR counterexample triangular solve and equal-residual/tie convention checked independently.

actual_item_dispositions.actual_use: Greedy CPQR initialization; full column rank, real/complex m>=n, 0<=k<n, f>=1, finite cap. Coefficient-first violating branch then residual-score branch; success only when all scores<=f.
Gram determinant rank-one update gives exact score as volume ratio. Row i of (R11 S)^-1 is row i of R11^-1 divided by Xij; continuity of the polynomial squared-volume identity handles Xij=0.

Every accepted swap has score>f>=1, so selected subset volume strictly increases and no subset recurs; at most binomial(n,k)-1 swaps. Success implies coefficient bound; smaller cap may return budget exhaustion.

Sum combined scores, set alpha=||R22||2/sigma_k(R11), use two block scalings and singular-value product inequality. This proves both stated comparisons with g=sqrt(1+f²k(n-k)), over real/complex fields, in exact arithmetic.

Kahan-style triangular 4x4 input c=1/2,s=sqrt(3)/2; equal residual norms and declared smallest-original-index tie produce identity permutation, then X1=-c(1+c)^2=-9/8. It refutes plain CPQR factor-one coefficient guarantee, not the combined-score procedure.
